semantic/architecture/separate-decisions.source: Microsoft .NET docs, "Architect Modern Web Applications with ASP.NET Core and Azure", Architectural principles: Separation of concerns
semantic/architecture/separate-decisions.note: States the same principle (keep business decisions separate from infrastructure/I-O so the business logic is easy to test), but at the layer/project level rather than per function.

semantic/architecture/thin-entry-points.source: Microsoft .NET docs, "Architect Modern Web Applications with ASP.NET Core and Azure", Develop ASP.NET Core MVC apps: Cross-cutting concerns
semantic/architecture/thin-entry-points.note: Says controller action methods (HTTP entry points) should be extremely thin once infrastructure and business logic are separated from the UI; the code example shows the intended shape. Framed for ASP.NET MVC actions only.

semantic/design/explicit-dependencies.source: Microsoft .NET docs, "Architect Modern Web Applications with ASP.NET Core and Azure", Architectural principles: Explicit dependencies
semantic/design/explicit-dependencies.note: The Explicit Dependencies Principle: methods and classes should require their collaborators through parameters/constructors instead of silently relying on global or infrastructure components. Direct equivalent.

semantic/design/no-flag-parameters.source: clean-code-javascript (Ryan McDermott), Functions: "Don't use flags as function parameters"
semantic/design/no-flag-parameters.note: Direct equivalent: a boolean parameter that switches code paths means the function does two things; split it. Includes the source's own bad/good example.

semantic/design/preserve-error-context.source: Uber Go Style Guide, Errors: Error Wrapping
semantic/design/preserve-error-context.note: Reused from the prior research session. Propagate the original error or add context naming the failed operation instead of a vague error.

semantic/design/single-responsibility.source: Microsoft .NET docs, "Architect Modern Web Applications with ASP.NET Core and Azure", Architectural principles: Single responsibility
semantic/design/single-responsibility.note: Objects should have one responsibility and one reason to change. Trimmed to the first paragraph; the following paragraphs apply the principle to layers and microservices. Speaks of objects/classes, not functions.

semantic/encapsulation/minimal-public-su.source: Google TypeScript Style Guide, Source file structure > Exports: Export visibility
semantic/encapsulation/minimal-public-su.note: Direct equivalent: only export what is used outside the module; minimize the exported API surface. HTML converted to Markdown (tags removed), text unchanged.

semantic/encapsulation/protect-internal-.source: Uber Go Style Guide, Guidelines: Copy Slices and Maps at Boundaries
semantic/encapsulation/protect-internal-.note: Covers both halves of the rule: storing a caller's mutable slice/map without copying, and returning internal slices/maps that expose internal state. Prose only; the bad/good HTML tables were trimmed. Go-specific (slices and maps).

semantic/maintainability/no-duplicated-k.source: Microsoft .NET docs, "Architect Modern Web Applications with ASP.NET Core and Azure", Architectural principles: Don't repeat yourself (DRY)
semantic/maintainability/no-duplicated-k.note: Direct equivalent: behavior for one concept specified in several places must all be updated when requirements change. The source's own note on coincidental duplication is kept verbatim.

semantic/naming/intent-revealing-names.source: Google TypeScript Style Guide, Naming: Descriptive names
semantic/naming/intent-revealing-names.note: Reused from the prior research session. Names must be descriptive and clear to a new reader, with the guide's own short-scope exception. Emphasis is more about clarity/abbreviation than about domain meaning. HTML converted to Markdown, text unchanged.

semantic/naming/names-match-behavior.source: Google TypeScript Style Guide, Language features > Classes: Getters and setters
semantic/naming/names-match-behavior.note: Partial equivalent: covers the "reads as a query but changes state" half of the rule, for TypeScript accessors only; nothing about names that understate a larger job. No redistributable guide states the general "names must not lie" rule in prose. HTML converted to Markdown, text unchanged.

semantic/organization/cohesive-modules.source: Google Go Style Guide, Best Practices: Package size
semantic/organization/cohesive-modules.note: Conceptually distinct things get their own package, and files should be focused enough that a maintainer can tell which file contains something, grouping related code by file. Trimmed to one sentence plus the file-size paragraph (cut before the doc.go remark). Partly about size, not only topic.

semantic/readability/comments-explain-wh.source: PEP 8 – Style Guide for Python Code, Comments and Inline Comments
semantic/readability/comments-explain-wh.note: Reused from the prior research session. Comments that contradict the code, and inline comments that state the obvious. reStructuredText code-block directives rendered as fenced code; text unchanged.

semantic/readability/consistent-abstract.source: clean-code-javascript (Ryan McDermott), Functions: "Functions should only be one level of abstraction"
semantic/readability/consistent-abstract.note: Direct equivalent of the rule name; the prose is short (the source relies on a long bad/good example, trimmed here).

semantic/readability/explain-magic-value.note: Unnamed constants ("magic strings and magic numbers") should be declared as named constants; includes the source's own example.

semantic/testing/descriptive-test-names.source: Microsoft .NET docs, Unit testing best practices for .NET: Follow test naming standards
semantic/testing/descriptive-test-names.note: Test names should state the method, the scenario, and the expected behavior. The before/after code-include directives were trimmed.

semantic/testing/test-behavior-not-imple.source: Microsoft .NET docs, Unit testing best practices for .NET: Validate private methods with public methods
semantic/testing/test-behavior-not-imple.note: Test through the public method rather than private implementation details. Trimmed to the opening and closing paragraphs (the example in between dropped). Does not mention mocks or call-count assertions.
